pl-l4d13c1-d1e115.summary: Asks whether wicked priests can confect this sacrament.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e118.summary: Answers that some, though wicked, truly consecrate, namely those who are within in name and sacrament though not in life, since it is effected not by the consecrator's merit but by the Creator's word.
claims: Wicked priests within the Church validly consecrate.
Consecration depends on the Creator's word, not merit.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: within the Catholic Church nothing more is done in the mystery by a good priest and nothing less by a bad, since it is accomplished not by the consecrator's merit but by the Creator's word and the Spirit's power; as Christ baptizes, so he makes his flesh and blood through the Spirit.
claims: Good and bad priests consecrate equally within the Church.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e131.summary: Quotes Gregory: some think communion less sanctified if given by those whose lives seem base, falling into a great snare, since one Spirit invisibly sanctifies the mysteries in the whole Church. He explains 'mystery' as hidden dispensation, 'sacrifice' as a sacred act consecrated in memory of the passion, and 'sacrament' as a celebration through which we receive something of what is signified, since divine power works salvation secretly under visible things; 'eucharist' means good grace. Whether given by good or bad ministers within the Church, it is holy, neither increased by good ministers' merits nor lessened by bad, since this power is divine, not human; the same holds of baptism and chrism.
claims: One Spirit sanctifies the sacraments throughout the Church.
The sacraments are neither increased nor diminished by the minister's merit.
Divine power works secretly under visible signs.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e140.summary: Holds that the excommunicated or those publicly marked as heretics, though priests, seem unable to confect this sacrament, since no one says in the consecration 'I offer' but 'we offer', as in the Church's person; so while other sacraments can be celebrated outside the Church, this one seemingly cannot.
claims: Excommunicated and heretical priests seem unable to consecrate.
The priest offers in the person of the Church.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e143.summary: Quotes Augustine: the Mass is so called because a heavenly messenger comes to consecrate the life-giving body, as the priest prays 'command these to be borne by your holy angel to your altar on high'; without the angel it cannot rightly be called Mass. Would God send an angel to consecrate a heretic's offering, having threatened 'I will curse your blessings'? If God curses and a simoniac blesses, which prevails?
claims: The angel does not come to consecrate a heretic's offering.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e155.summary: Quotes Gregory on 'I will curse your blessings': what you possess by my blessings, or whatever you bless; because they do not bless the saints from a true heart, or because they bless evildoers and flatter sinners who are rich.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e164.summary: Quotes Jerome: 'I will curse your blessings' means whatever you bless will be cursed by me.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e173.summary: Concludes that a heretic cut off from Catholic unity cannot confect this sacrament, since the holy angels who attend its celebration are not present when a heretic or simoniac presumes to profane it; where the mysteries of the Lord's body and blood are performed, the assembly of the heavenly citizens is surely present.
claims: A heretic cut off from the Church cannot confect the eucharist.
Angels attend the eucharistic celebration.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e177.summary: States that in completing this mystery the form must be kept, the order held, that is, the minister must be a priest, and the intention to do it must be present.
claims: The eucharist requires form, priestly order, and intention.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e180.summary: Asks whether one who does not believe about the mystery as the truth holds can intend to confect it, and if he does not intend it, whether he confects it.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e183.summary: Reports some who say that even one who does not believe rightly can intend, not to confect it, which would already be to believe rightly, but to do what others do when it is confected; and so the intention is present, and even if he is said to lack the intention of confecting, since he intends to say and do what others do, the mystery is accomplished.
claims: Intending to do what others do suffices for validity.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e186.summary: Adds that it can soundly be said that brute animals do not receive Christ's body, though they seem to. What then does a mouse take and eat? God knows.
claims: Animals do not receive Christ's body.

pl-l4d13c1-d1e189.summary: Closes: we have touched on some things about this heavenly mystery to be faithfully held by Catholics; whoever contradicts them is judged a heretic.
claims: Contradicting this teaching is heresy.

pl-l4d13c1.summary: Asks whether wicked priests can confect the sacrament. Those within the Church, though wicked, truly consecrate, since it is done not by the consecrator's merit but by the Creator's word, as Augustine and Gregory teach: the same Spirit sanctifies in all, and the sacraments are neither enlarged by good ministers nor diminished by bad. But the excommunicated or manifest heretics, though priests, seem unable to confect it, since the priest says 'we offer' in the person of the Church; Augustine says the angel who consecrates does not come to a heretic, and Gregory and Jerome read 'I will curse your blessings' accordingly. The form must be kept, the minister must be a priest, and the intention must be present; even one who misbelieves may intend to do what others do. Animals that seem to eat the host do not receive Christ's body; God knows what a mouse eats. Those who contradict this teaching are judged heretics.
claims: Wicked priests within the Church validly consecrate.
The sacrament is effected by the Creator's word, not the minister's merit.
Excommunicated and heretical priests seem unable to consecrate, since they cannot offer in the Church's person.
The eucharist requires form, priestly order, and intention.
One who misbelieves can still intend to do what the Church does.
Animals do not receive Christ's body.
